content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to set up hardware using a [product_name] with more than one ethernet port? I want to connect two devices to the [product_name] without using an ethernet switch. The setup also needs to meet DNV certification requirements. Thank you in advance.

This is not feasible. The [product_name] only has one ethernet port and doesn't act as a switch. You'll need an external switch or router. For reference, the [article_no] supports up to 16 ethernet connections, but only through its single port. Please tell us which devices you want to connect to the [product_name].
Could you explain what a DNV certificate is?
It's a certificate related to shipbuilding. See [url] for details.

Hello, I want to connect an HMI (not from [company_name]) to the [product_name], but also keep ethernet connectivity for both the [product_name] and the HMI. Both have only one ethernet port, and there’s just one ethernet outlet available in the room. The entire setup should have DNV certification as it's for use on a ship.

The document you linked lists all [company_name] components with this certificate, but the [product_name] isn't included. It only has a single Ethernet port (RJ45), and if the HMI also has one port, an external switch is necessary. The document lists certified switches as well.
[product_name] has the certificate: [url] However, I couldn't find certification for the CMS modules. I'm looking for an alternative solution as they may not be certified.
I've attached a section from the manual which might provide further guidance.

I understand that multiple devices could be connected if there were additional ethernet ports available. However, currently, both the [product_name] and the HMI only have one port, and the whole solution needs DNV certification. If certification wasn't required, I could use CSM modules. I’m not sure how to proceed—do you have any suggestions?

You could use a Scalance switch instead of the CSM module since it's certified. Here's a product link: SCALANCE – network components for industrial communication. Also, I've attached the datasheet for the Scalance switch X005.
Is the Scalance switch compatible with a regular [product_name]? I thought it was only compatible with [version_no].
I haven't used a Scalance switch, but it should work fine with the [product_name]. It's just an unmanaged switch. The CSM module also isn't limited to only [product_name] use.

Is the CSM module considered an expansion module for the [product_name]? [url] I thought the X005 was an expansion for [version_no], but if it's a standalone switch, can I connect non-[company_name] devices to it? Appreciate your help, [user_name].

The CSM module has the same housing as the [product_name], suitable for installation in compact units, but is not exclusive to the [product_name]. For example, I personally use a TP-Link Gigabit switch (TL-SG 108E) with my [product_name] devices. A switch works regardless of brand.

Hello [user_name], Privately I use inexpensive TP-Link hubs. At work, I use [company_name] Scalance switches because they meet DNV requirements for shipboard use. The Scalance switch is advantageous due to its 24V power supply and wide temperature range. As [user_name] mentioned, a switch is a switch, but for industrial applications aboard ships, reliable equipment is preferable due to power and temperature concerns.

Hi, Is it possible to add two [product_name] TDE modules since you have three devices to connect? By adding two [product_name] TDEs, you'd have two extra Ethernet ports. Would this resolve your connectivity issue?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to expand network connectivity for a [product_name] device that only has one ethernet port, and lack built-in switch capability. The main challenge is complying with DNV certification while connecting multiple devices, especially in environments with limited ethernet outlets such as ship rooms. Recommendations involve using certified external switches like Scalance, which introduces additional complexity in constrained spaces.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to allow multiple direct ethernet connections or to have a certified way to connect additional devices to a single port, without needing external uncertified switches.
